source: Muse recheck of first-pass flags; apply through the belt (02 fact block -> 16 -> 04/05 remint), never in place

corrections.corrected_statement: Connecticut law requires any first time applicant of any age who has not previously held a license to complete an eight hour Safe Driving Practices course before obtaining a license.
corrections.note: Removed the two hour parent requirement not stated on the provided pages.

corrections.corrected_statement: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance and make turning harder when the road is wet, so check tires for wear and damage once every month and before a long trip and check pressure with a gauge using the manual or door jamb recommendation.
corrections.note: Fixed timing to apply monthly checks to wear and damage, not to pressure.

corrections.corrected_statement: Place Lincoln head first into the lowest tread groove and if any part of the head is covered you have safe tread but if tread is lower grip in bad weather is greatly reduced.
corrections.note: Removed replace order, kept only reduced grip for low tread.

corrections.corrected_statement: A driver of any age may use a phone in an emergency to call responders hospitals clinics and police or fire departments and a driver eighteen years of age or older who is a peace officer firefighter or ambulance driver may use a handheld phone.
corrections.note: Removed on duty limit not stated on page.

corrections.corrected_statement: If any part of Lincoln head is covered by tread you have safe tread but if tread falls below that level grip in bad conditions is greatly reduced.
corrections.note: Removed order for new tires, kept only reduced grip.

corrections.corrected_statement: Groups at special risk for fatigue related crashes include young adults sixteen to twenty four years old who often need more sleep and people with untreated obstructive sleep apnea who are seven times more likely to fall asleep at the wheel and night shift workers whose risk increases by nearly six times while rotating shift workers and people working more than sixty hours a week need to be particularly careful.
corrections.note: Corrected to limit nearly six times risk to night shift work only.

corrections.corrected_statement: Young adults sixteen to twenty four years old often need more sleep and people with untreated obstructive sleep apnea are seven times more likely to fall asleep at the wheel and night shift work increases risk by nearly six times while rotating shift workers and people working more than sixty hours a week need to be particularly careful.
corrections.note: Corrected to limit nearly six times risk to night shift work only.

corrections.corrected_statement: If you run over a shoulder rumble strip pull off the road at a safe place immediately and check your alertness level and if you are not feeling well let someone else drive and avoid alcohol and sedating medications by checking labels or asking your doctor and when emotions affect driving calm down and stay off the road until calm or have someone else drive.
corrections.note: Corrected medication guidance to avoid and check labels rather than handover.

corrections.corrected_statement: Someone under eighteen who commits negligent homicide with a motor vehicle, evading responsibility after a crash that causes death or serious injury, or driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs cannot be considered a youthful offender.
corrections.note: Added missing serious injury and drugs scope to the bar list.

corrections.corrected_statement: Someone under eighteen who commits negligent homicide with a motor vehicle, evading responsibility after a crash causing death or serious injury, or driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs cannot be a youthful offender, while youthful offender records for reckless driving, driving while suspended, evading after property damage or nonserious injury, street racing, or eluding police must be disclosed to the Department of Motor Vehicles for suspension.
corrections.note: Added missing serious injury and alcohol or drugs scope to the bar list.

corrections.corrected_statement: Anyone age twenty four or younger who commits two or more moving violations or suspension violations and anyone age twenty five or older who has three or more such convictions must complete certified operator retraining, and an additional moving violation within three years after completion results in license suspension of at least thirty days.
corrections.note: Fixed age threshold to twenty five or older and added two or more, three or more, and at least qualifiers.

corrections.corrected_statement: If your brakes stop working pump the brake pedal several times then use the parking brake slowly without locking the rear wheels then shift to lower gears to stop off the roadway, and if a tire blows out hold the steering wheel tightly to keep going straight take your foot off the gas and brake lightly then pull off the road in a safe place.
corrections.note: Removed locked line and added correct hold straight with light braking and correct brake failure sequence.

corrections.corrected_statement: To avoid a collision you may stop or turn or speed up, and speeding up is best or necessary when another vehicle is about to hit you from the side or from behind and there is room to the front to get out of danger.
corrections.note: Removed ranking of stopping and turning first that the page does not state.

corrections.corrected_statement: When required to stop because of a sign or signal you must stop before your vehicle reaches the stop line and you must yield to pedestrians in or about to enter a crosswalk and not all crosswalks are marked so be alert for pedestrians when crossing intersections.
corrections.note: Removed every corner claim and restored be alert at intersections limit.

corrections.corrected_statement: Shared center lanes are reserved for making left turns and can be used by vehicles traveling in both directions but in some areas become a reversible lane during rush hours and reversible lanes carry traffic in one direction at certain times and in the opposite direction at other times under a green arrow for use and a red X for no use.
corrections.note: Removed all day and restored rush hours reversible exception.

corrections.corrected_statement: When required to stop because of a sign or signal you must stop before your vehicle reaches the stop line and you must yield to pedestrians in or about to enter a crosswalk and not all crosswalks are marked.
corrections.note: Removed claim that stop line duty survives missing paint.

corrections.corrected_statement: A solid red HAWK signal means pedestrians are in the crosswalk and motorists must stop and a flashing red HAWK signal means drivers must stop but may proceed when pedestrians have cleared the crosswalk like an ordinary flashing red light that means the same as a stop sign requiring a full stop before proceeding when safe.
corrections.note: Added required stop for flashing red and removed reverse claim.

corrections.corrected_statement: Signs posted before turns and curves use the shape of the arrow to tell what to expect and may have a small sign below showing the maximum safe speed, while guide signs that tell where you are and how to get where you want to go are mostly rectangular.
corrections.note: Removed unsupported tall and fixed arrow wording to match page.

corrections.corrected_statement: For adults of eighteen or more the donor registry counts as legal donation authorization, so tell family and read more at ct.gov/dmv.
corrections.note: Legal-authorization rule is on page 10, but family notice and website detail are on page 11.

corrections.corrected_statement: Motorcycle operators may use a complete lane with two motorcycles allowed to share one lane, so check mirrors and blind spots by turning your head because approximately one half of crashes involve another vehicle and nearly forty percent are caused by another vehicle turning left in front of the motorcycle, requiring careful looks for motorcycles before turning left.
corrections.note: Removed claim that riders mostly die from left hooks and stated actual crash shares.

corrections.corrected_statement: Trucks crawl uphill, swing wide, brake long and tip tall, so human error by car drivers can still wreck the evading trucker: shun every No-Zone.
corrections.note: Uphill speed loss is stated on adjacent page twenty, not page twenty one.

corrections.corrected_statement: Safer drivers look at least twelve seconds ahead, which is about one block in the city and about four blocks on the highway.
corrections.note: Removed four second sight rule because it is not on the allowed pages.

corrections.corrected_statement: Before turning left yield to all oncoming traffic including bicycles and check oncoming traffic again before turning, and before turning right on red after stopping check traffic from the left and oncoming turning traffic and pedestrians and do not turn immediately after passing a bicycle unless a sign prohibits the turn.
corrections.note: Added missing oncoming turning traffic, pedestrian and bicycle timing checks.

corrections.corrected_statement: You may pass slow moving bicycles in a no passing zone only when you can do so safely with enough sight distance, and you must not stop park or drive in a bicycle lane unless entering or leaving an alley or driveway or performing official duties or directed by a police officer or in an emergency while yielding to bicycles.
corrections.note: Added missing alley, official duty and police direction exceptions.
